name: std/text
description: Text: the string family and its pool, UTF-8, regular expressions, and number conversion into and out of strings.
residual: Format arrived 2026-09-03. Every other language spells this printf and printf needs varargs, which Active Oberon does not have and should not grow for this; what it has is objects, so the template is an object and the arguments arrive as calls on it. The shape of a message stays in one string -- greppable, translatable -- and each argument keeps the type the compiler checked. A hole nobody filled is written out as {} rather than swallowed, and Complete says so.

Unicode arrived 2026-09-03 and is generated, not written: tests/gen-unicode.py turns data/UnicodeData.txt into a run table -- 2642 runs over the whole code space, 151 distinct (category, case) values -- so the character database finally travels in a headless SDK. UnicodeProperties parses that same file at run time through Texts and Codecs, which is why it is in lib/texts and this is not. Simple case mapping only, and the file in the tree is Unicode 5.0: a newer table is a newer file plus one script run.

Regex arrived 2026-09-03: the library had no regular expressions at all, and it is here rather than in the registry because a pattern is a shared type -- two packages that each ship their own matcher cannot hand one to the other. It is Thompson's construction, so the cost is O(pattern * input) with no pattern able to make it worse; the price of that is no back references. Bytes, not characters: the UCD tables are still missing (see below), so a range cannot span a multi-byte character.

The modules under `graphical` belong to this package but cannot travel in the headless SDK: their own import closure reaches the window system. The list is checked against the import graph by docker/gen-headless-core.sh, so it cannot go quietly out of date.

Re-homed 2026-08-27 by the shared-type rule (docs/STDLIB.md): a package holds what other packages talk to each other through. See that file for what moved where and why. In: Strings, UTF8Strings, DynamicStrings, StringPool, TFStringPool from std/base; UnicodeProperties and UnicodeBidirectionality from std/ime. RealConversions did NOT come: Streams imports it, so it stays in std/base and the dependency runs text -> base only.

UnicodeProperties and UnicodeBidirectionality are graphical; Texts is not, which the gate had to tell me. They read their tables through Texts AND Codecs, and it is Codecs that reaches the window system. Making them headless means giving them a reader that is not the rich-text model -- the same work as regenerating the tables from the UCD.

Out on 2026-08-27: Texts, UnicodeProperties and UnicodeBidirectionality to lib/texts. Texts is the rich-text piece-list model -- an editor's document, not the string layer -- and it is what dragged WMEvents, FP1616 and the whole XML stack into the payload. The two Unicode modules follow it because they read their tables through it. The character database belongs in std/text; this implementation of it does not, and the way back is to regenerate the tables from the UCD with a plain reader.
